title: How to Eradicate Ebola?

limitations: All 36 pages were rendered and visually reviewed.
OCR damages several Greek symbols and matrix entries; visual transcription is retained with medium confidence.
The source uses unit dose as a proxy because actual drug dosage is unavailable.

deliverables: Fit baseline and improved Ebola spread models.
Estimate medicine quantity and delivery locations.
Evaluate manufacturing speed, medicine efficacy, corpse handling, and contact tracing.
Define control and eradication conditions and sensitivity.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: No official problem statement was located; author prose reconstructs deliverables and never reclassifies the path-derived A label.

section_map.summary: Problem background, prior research, and a five-part work roadmap.
SEIR baseline, data fit, and improved SEIHCR(CT) model.
Corpse handling, contact tracing, and local conclusion.
Derivative control region and eradication timing.

section_map.section: Letter to the World Medical Association

contributions.summary: Adds hospitalized infectious cases, contaminated corpses, and contact tracing to SEIR.
Uses cumulative burden and growth rate to estimate daily unit-dose demand.
Weights fuzzy c-means by city medicine demand to select six headquarters.
Defines derivative-based control and plateau-based eradication conditions.

MU-A-2015-32150-002 -> MU-A-2015-32150-003: time-varying transmission initializes improved compartment model

feedbacks: Fit quality motivates the improved model.
Sensitivity and weaknesses bound the policy interpretation.
dependency_graph.closure_status: The paper has a visible epidemic-model -> supply -> delivery -> intervention -> control/eradication route, but external operational validation remains incomplete.

assumptions.summary: Country populations are modeled as closed compartments over the study horizon.
Medicine is provided in hospitals and changes recovery/fatality parameters.
Cities can receive direct straight-line deliveries from selected centers.
Unit dose represents demand because actual pharmacological dosage is unavailable.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Reported cumulative cases calibrate and compare the SEIR baseline.
Guinea, Sierra Leone, and Liberia use country-specific populations and rates.
CUM and growth rate are transformed into unit-dose demand.
City coordinates and demand weights enter weighted fuzzy c-means.

models.summary: Baseline compartment model and differential equations.
Improved compartment model with hospital, corpse, and tracing pathways.
Demand-weighted geographic clustering for delivery headquarters.

verification.summary: Calculated curves are compared with WHO reported curves.
SEIHCR(CT) curves are compared with cumulative case data.
Objective decrease and inflection motivate six clusters.
Perturbation plots test transmission, incubation, and hospital fatality effects.

results_trace.summary: The improved model is reported to fit the outbreak better than SEIR.
Daily unit-dose demand is calculated from cumulative cases and growth.
Six headquarters are mapped to city groups.
Capacity above average daily demand is associated with lower hospital fatality.
Earlier intervention and higher efficacy reduce eradication time.

writing_logic.summary: Mission -> prior research -> named work route.
Baseline SEIR -> fit -> improved mechanisms -> parameter choice.
Cumulative cases -> medicine quantity -> delivery -> capacity and efficacy.
Control region -> eradication timing -> sensitivity -> limitations -> memo.

language_observations.summary: Ordinal transitions route the reader through a multi-stage method.
Baseline limitation is followed by explicit mechanism additions.
Missing dosage data is converted into a transparent proxy.
A verbal policy concept is defined through derivative conditions.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Matched calculated/reported curves plausibly support auditability, but award status alone cannot establish causality.

weaknesses.summary: Many coupled parameters may be weakly identifiable.
Only Freetown receives detailed city-level illustration.
Distance scaling, initialization, and logistics constraints are incomplete.
Thresholds and WMA recommendations lack external operational validation.

independent_extensions.summary: Re-estimate the full model with joint uncertainty and country-level hierarchical effects.
Add capacity, routing, stock, and cold-chain constraints to delivery optimization.

unresolved_questions: Parameter values are partly borrowed or fitted without complete reproducible optimization details.
The six-center selection lacks initialization and logistics sensitivity.
Unit dose is a proxy rather than a pharmacological dosage.
Control thresholds depend on selected parameters and finite-difference interpretation.
The WMA policy translation has no external implementation validation.
